headline: Cadia disruption lifts costs; guidance, buybacks hold
summary_short: Newmont reported Q2 2026 revenue of $6.12 billion and net income of $2.20 billion ($2.06 diluted EPS), down from Q1 as lower gold prices and Cadia's seismic downtime lifted AISC to $1,621/oz. Free cash flow was still a Q2 record at $2.2 billion; full-year 2026 guidance stays on track.
summary_long: Revenue fell 16% q/q to $6.12B and net income dropped 33% to $2.20B ($2.06 diluted EPS) as average realized gold price slipped $486/oz and Cadia's April seismic events cut copper, gold and by-product output. Gold by-product AISC jumped 58% to $1,621/oz on lower volumes, softer silver pricing, higher Ghana royalties and diesel costs, plus incremental Cadia downtime spend. Free cash flow was $2.2B, still a Q2 record, funding $1.7B of buybacks and a $0.26/share dividend since the last call. Cash rose to $9.0B (net cash $3.4B). Full-year 2026 production, cost and capital guidance is unchanged and on track.

drivers.explanation: Lower average realized gold price (-$486/oz q/q) and reduced base-metal volumes after Cadia's seismic-event downtime cut consolidated sales versus Q1.
Cadia's April seismic events curtailed output, plus planned lower-grade sequencing at Ahafo South, Peñasquito and Yanacocha; partly offset by higher Lihir and Boddington production.

Cost per ounce rose on lower gold/co-product volumes, softer silver pricing, a full quarter of higher Ghana royalties, higher diesel prices and incremental Cadia downtime costs, partly offset by higher copper pricing.
Lower revenue from weaker realized gold and silver prices drove the $1.1B q/q decline, partly offset by a $452M drop in income and mining tax expense.
Lower operating cash flow and higher capital investment reduced FCF, partly offset by a smaller unfavorable working-capital swing than Q1.

Management frames the quarter as strong operational and financial execution despite the Cadia disruption: record Q2 free cash flow, $1.9B of shareholder returns since the last call, and full-year 2026 guidance reaffirmed unchanged.

Newmont discloses Costs Applicable to Sales (CAS) and All-In Sustaining Cost (AISC) on a by-product and co-product basis; it does not report a separate C1 cash cost metric (that convention is more common at copper-primary miners), so AISC by-product ($1,621/oz) is used as the primary unit-cost KPI here — not conflated with CAS ($1,043/oz by-product). Silver, copper, lead and zinc are co-products netted as by-product credits against gold costs per the company's own methodology. 'Adjusted EBITDA' ($3,757M) is the release's own non-GAAP figure and differs from the shard's structured-feed 'ebitda_usd_m' ($3,638M, Yahoo-timeseries) — different definitions, both sourced, not reconciled. Basic/diluted EPS ($2.07/$2.06) reconcile exactly to the SEC-verbatim shard values. The $1.7B buyback figure covers the period since the last earnings call (Apr 23-Jul 23, 2026), not a clean calendar quarter, per the release's own framing. All eight FY2026 guidance line items (production, AISC, CAS, sustaining/development capex, copper/silver/zinc production) are carried as move='held': the release states full-year guidance 'remains on track' and, for sustaining/development capital specifically, 'remaining unchanged' from the Feb 19, 2026 issuance — no numeric change was stated for any line.
